reports.evidenceNotes: Next check: repeat the jam-clear sequence and record the result.

reports.summary: QA report: Focus on Shooter and Transfer geometry — The transfer path clears through full extension. Recheck it after the fasteners are torqued so we know the gap holds.
reports.notes: The transfer path clears through full extension. Recheck it after the fasteners are torqued so we know the gap holds.
reports.evidenceNotes: Follow-up: verify transfer clearance after final torque.

reports.summary: QA report: Finish Block CAD — The interference review is clear so far. I left drawing sign-off open for one more look before release.
reports.notes: The interference review is clear so far. I left drawing sign-off open for one more look before release.
reports.evidenceNotes: Follow-up: get a second look at the drawing before sign-off.

reports.summary: QA report: Prototype working intake — The left side is not picking up as cleanly as the right. I want to try a small guide adjustment and run the same feed again.
reports.notes: The left side is not picking up as cleanly as the right. I want to try a small guide adjustment and run the same feed again.
reports.evidenceNotes: Follow-up: adjust the guide and compare another feed run.

reports.summary: QA report: Base code updated to 2026 — The autonomous timeout is still short of the target. I changed the timing and need to run the routine again in simulation.
reports.notes: The autonomous timeout is still short of the target. I changed the timing and need to run the routine again in simulation.
reports.evidenceNotes: Follow-up: rerun the autonomous routine after the timing change.

reports.summary: QA report: Design review (intake/conveyor) — The transfer has a small dead zone between the intake and conveyor. We should compare two guide angles before locking the layout.
reports.notes: The transfer has a small dead zone between the intake and conveyor. We should compare two guide angles before locking the layout.
reports.evidenceNotes: Follow-up: compare guide angles and confirm continuous handoff.

reports.notes: Belt tracking looks steady and the connectors are labeled. We should revisit strain relief before the handoff.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: check strain relief during the conveyor handoff.

reports.notes: We need a tighter handoff plan for the conveyor work. I put the remaining owners and dates in one place so we can reset the sequence.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: confirm the revised owners and dates with the group.

reports.notes: Most of the intake checks are done. Connector strain is the one item I would like to test again before we call it ready.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: repeat the connector strain check.

reports.notes: We reviewed the subsystem readiness list and still have one area to work through together.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: close the remaining subsystem discussion.

reports.notes: The corner fit is close. I marked one seam for another pass before the bumpers go on.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: recheck corner alignment and finish the seam.

reports.notes: We ran the autonomous routines in simulation and found one sequence to repeat on the practice field.
reports.evidenceNotes: Next review: run the sequence on the practice field.

workLogs.notes: I ran the intake through the test pieces and cleared one jam between runs. It fed cleanly after I reset the guide.
We finished the intake assembly and checked the roller spacing before packing up. I marked the loose side plate for a quick look next meeting.
I routed the Quest wiring with the rest of the harness and tied it back so it stays clear of the moving parts.
Countersunk the intake roller bolts and checked that the heads sat below the plate. The roller turns without catching now.
I moved the robot improvement items into order and checked the next handoffs with the subsystem group.
I sorted the recent packages and matched the labels to the order list so we could find everything later.
I went through the remaining purchase list and checked the quantities before sending it back for approval.
I helped get the interview questions in order and made sure we had time for each section.
I finished the paper form and checked that the online version asked for the same information.
I added the event notes to the impact folder and cleaned up the captions so we can find the photos by activity.
I made the next button batch and checked it against the spreadsheet quotas before putting the boxes away.
I restocked the outreach bag and packed the handouts and table supplies for the next event.
I sorted the robot reveal photos and clips into one folder and picked a few that show the whole build.
I trimmed the video and checked the caption on my phone before saving the post draft.
I pulled together the clips for the media post and sent the final version over for a look.
I compared the game notes with the routes we had discussed and wrote down two questions for the next strategy session.
I went through the scouting fields and practiced entering a match so I know what to watch for.
I drafted the pit questions and grouped them by what we need to learn before a match.
I walked through the shop setup and practiced the safety check before starting the next build activity.
I helped set up the training activity and wrote down the steps that were easiest to miss.
I practiced the presentation and shortened the opening so we could leave more time for questions.
